chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

In prayer, reciting the following words upon turning towards Allah will suffice for you: 'I have turned my face towards He who created the heavens and the earth,' following the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, a Muslim, 'and I am not of the polytheists,' 'Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds; no partner has He, and I have been commanded this,' 'and I am of the Muslims.' And one Takbir will suffice for you.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite during the first ruku' of the prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt provides a concise alternative to the lengthy opening supplication (Du'a al-Iftitah) for the Imam during Ruku', emphasizing the core declaration of monotheism (Tawhid). It explicitly links the prayer ritual to the Hanif faith of Prophet Ibrahim, reinforcing the Shia practice of dedicating one's entire existence—prayer, sacrifice, life, and death—to Allah alone. This brevity highlights the principle that sincerity and correct intention in turning towards Allah are sufficient for the validity of this specific act of worship.
